key_insight: This paper introduces COSA-GS, a practical compression approach for 3D Gaussian Splatting that avoids fragile spatial context modeling while keeping compression effective. The core idea is to make coding more robust and deployment-friendly by reducing complexity and eliminating cross-platform numerical inconsistencies.
problem_solved: 3D Gaussian Splatting offers high-quality novel-view synthesis, but its large storage cost makes it hard to use in practice. Existing compression methods often depend on irregular 3D spatial context and floating-point inference, which increases training/coding complexity and can cause entropy-decoding failures across platforms.
method: Constructs context without relying on spatial aggregation over irregular 3D structures.
Reduces dependence on floating-point context inference to improve numerical consistency across platforms.
Targets practical entropy coding and compression efficiency for 3DGS representations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work makes 3DGS more deployable by improving compression reliability and reducing storage overhead. It is especially relevant for real-world systems where reproducibility, portability, and efficient decoding matter.

paper_title: Towards Practical Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting
